your_note: Added Basic/Bearer schemes and set credential_gate because working access is tied to the trial or a paid account.

your_note: Gladly requires an active commercial customer account; an admin must then grant API User permission.
agent_notes: API access requires an active commercial Gladly customer account and admin privileges to generate API tokens. Uses API tokens (bearer tokens) generated from the Gladly admin settings to authenticate REST API requests.

your_note: Added API key auth, removed websocket (Aircall documents REST plus webhooks), and recorded the trial credential gate.
agent_notes: Developers can sign up for a free trial to access developer tools and test the API, but full API usage requires a paid plan (Essentials, Professional, or Enterprise starting at $30-$50/license/month) OAuth2 auth code flow for public marketplace apps; HTTP Basic Auth (using api_id and api_token) or Bearer token for private apps and customer integrations

your_note: Twilio now publishes an official hosted MCP documentation server.
agent_notes: Developers can sign up for a free trial account instantly with no credit card required to obtain API credentials. HTTP Basic authentication using Account SID and Auth Token, or API Key SID and Secret.

agent_notes: Developers can create a Meta app for free on the Meta for Developers platform and select the Threads use case; advanced access for live users requires app review. OAuth 2.0 protocol using short-lived and long-lived Threads user access tokens acquired via the Authorization Window.

your_note: systeme.io now documents and hosts its own MCP server.

agent_notes: Developers can sign up for a free Ecwid account to set up a development environment and obtain access tokens or create apps. OAuth2 authorization code flow for public apps; access tokens / secret tokens for private apps.

OAuth2 auth code flow for public apps; static access tokens (X-Auth-Token header) and client IDs for store/account level accounts; JWTs for storefront and customer auth.

your_note: SE Ranking offers a 14-day API trial and now includes an official remote MCP server.
agent_notes: API access is available on higher-tier plans (Pro and Business) or via specialized API pricing packages requiring a paid subscription. The SE Ranking API uses an API key (access token) passed with requests to authenticate.

your_note: Removed sdk_or_cli_only because Vercel exposes a public documented REST API.

Uses Vercel Access Tokens passed as a Bearer token in the Authorization header for personal/team resource access, and OAuth2 for public marketplace integrations.

your_note: Added bearer-token authentication, removed sdk_or_cli_only, and recorded Snowflake managed MCP as official.
agent_notes: Developers can sign up for a self-serve trial account, which provides API and database access. Supports OAuth, key-pair authentication (JWT), and workload identity federation (AWS, Azure, GCP, OIDC).

your_note: Removed sdk_or_cli_only because Asana exposes a documented REST API.

Supports Personal Access Tokens (PATs) for quick/single-user scripts, Service Accounts (enterprise feature), and OAuth 2.0 for multi-user applications.

your_note: Airtable now publishes an official remote MCP server.
agent_notes: Developers can sign up for a free Airtable account and generate personal access tokens or configure OAuth integrations self-serve. OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for public integrations; personal access tokens (bearer tokens) for private scripts and individual use.
